megh-114.title: The 2010 Chile earthquake
megh-114.text: On 27 February 2010, a magnitude 8.8 earthquake struck central Chile. Its waves set off seiches as far away as Louisiana. Nearby, the Caldera del Atuel and other volcanic centres subsided after the quake. Great earthquakes along this coast often stir its volcanoes, as {{ref:megh-095}} showed half a century earlier.

megh-069.title: The Laki fissure poisons Iceland
megh-069.text: About a fifth of Iceland's people died after the Laki eruption. From June 1783 to February 1784, the 40 km Laki fissure poured out about 15 km³ of lava. It was one of history's largest effusive eruptions, those that pour out lava rather than explode. Its lava fields cover 565 km² of southeast Iceland. Fluorine and chlorine poisoning devastated farming. The eruption released about 120 million tonnes of sulfur dioxide. In Northern Hemisphere ice cores its sulfate signal exceeds even that of Samalas, and the sulfur caused substantial cooling. Famine cost Egypt a sixth of its people in 1784, and hardship in Europe may have fed the French Revolution.

megh-124.title: The 2025 Kamchatka earthquake
megh-124.text: The Kamchatka coast shook again in 2025. Another giant megathrust earthquake, of magnitude 8.8, struck where the Pacific plate subducts along the Kuril–Kamchatka Trench. It was the same boundary that broke in {{ref:megh-091}}, a fault with a long record of giant quakes. Its return is a reminder that these plate boundaries reload and fail again.
